newsitem.title: UK: Gold Outlook-Prices forecast to edge lower.
newsitem.headline: Gold Outlook-Prices forecast to edge lower.

text.p: Precious metal dealers were looking for prices to move lower this week after last Friday's Comex options expiry.

The gold market's week-long consolidation effectively ground to a halt ahead of the expiry at the end of last week. "The options players have gold in a stranglehold," one dealer said on Friday referring to the yellow metal's narrow price bracket.
Gold fixed on Friday at $353.00 per ounce and $352.90, up from a fix at the start of the week of $349.90.
"There is a lot of uncertainty about direction," one dealer, but others saw the price coming off a bit this week before the market gathered steam for another try on the upside.
"The upside has been quite thoroughly tested last week without making much of an impression," one dealer said.
Dealers noted liquidity was readily available and sub one percent one-month lease rates suggested most of the short positions in the market since early this year had been covered.

Silver attracted what some dealers considered technically related fund buying last Thursday when a "golden cross" formed on the chart where the 50 day moving average crossed the 200 day as both lines ascended. This is usually seen as a bullish signal.
Even so, follow-through buying was outweighed by sell offers. "It still looks pretty well capped around $5.32 and there is a problem with offers coming in at $5.30," one dealer said.

If silver broke above $5.32 however, it could run up to $5.45, a dealer said. Platinum and palladium were noticeably less volatile late last week than for some time leading some dealers to opine that they were running out of steam. A report late on Thursday said that U.S. car makers had not revised palladium purchasing plans despite the market's 37 percent rise since its low last November. Palladium prices have held since Russia's Almaz export agency said the same day it would probably begin exports for this year later this month.
The markets have been buoyed by a delayed start to Russian-Japanese supply contract talks and the complete halt in Russian exports since December.
Russia is the largest exporter of palladium and Japan the largest importer of the rare white metal.
Dealers and analysts said the statement probably referred to spot sales and that their volume was much more significant than their timing.
Meanwhile some U.S.-based funds are known to be long of the metal and supposedly are in for the long term, dealers said.
However one noted, "Palladium is at the mercy of the funds now."

Palladium had its final fix on Friday at $152.25 having opened the week at $148.50 and platinum was rated at $382.75 against a fix last Monday at $378.00. --Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
